tasks.short: Investigate species adaptability to changed environmental conditions

steps.what: Define adaptability questions and critically review species evidence against the changed environmental conditions
Investigate animal and plant responses through observations, experiments and interpretation of adaptability evidence

tasks.design: Retain critical evidence review and species investigation with the ecologist, using {DOCS} and the {OTHER} ecological research and observation environment. The ecologist designs observations or experiments and interprets what they establish about adaptability, rather than accepting a generated species-suitability label.
tasks.previous_blocker: Responses depend on life stage, interacting stressors, population differences and the conditions actually observed.
tasks.enabler_now: Search and analysis tools support the investigation, but the supplied digest does not demonstrate a repeatable reduction in this scientific work.
tasks.still_hard: Short-term survival or a related species' response may not establish long-term adaptability in the target environment.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist identifies which observations distinguish genuine adaptation from temporary tolerance or confounding conditions.
tasks.altitude: Scientific investigation effort and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Design observations that distinguish survival from sustained population performance
reach.learn: Life-stage effects, confounding stressors and evidence transfer limits

evidence.claim: Retaining critical species evidence assessment and empirical investigation is a model-knowledge boundary; general literature summaries and environmental data platforms do not establish species adaptability or task savings.

assumptions: Boundary is scientific review, investigation design and empirical interpretation, ending at research findings rather than conservation or land-use authorisation.

Published study authors and site specialists supply existing evidence. In fully retained s1 the ecologist captures target species, changed conditions, study context, comparison questions and evidence gaps; no ready adaptable-species flag is presumed.

The ecologist and research collaborators produce new observations during s2 after the investigation design exists. Focal-role observation, enquiry, interpretation and finding capture remain fully counted; collaborator work stays in its original workflow without a claimed saving.
Missing or incomparable evidence leads to manual reading, further observation or experiments rather than automatic extrapolation. Test existing research functions before any custom tool.

OTHER denotes ecological research and observation software. This design introduces no new automation, data contract or capture requirement, so incremental upkeep is zero; existing analytical runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Need for laboratory versus field investigation
research_questions: Which findings would distinguish temporary tolerance from sustained adaptability under the specified changed conditions?

already_counted.description: Critical evidence review and investigation design
Empirical investigation and interpretation of adaptability

incremental.description: No additional automation or capture upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net zero with zero incremental upkeep. Scientific reading, observations and interpretation retain their full time; no routine screening or reporting baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Species investigation and scientific interpretation remain unchanged.
reach: Work with ecological researchers on representative response evidence
role.ambitious_version: An ecologist who explains precisely what observations do and do not establish about species adaptability.
